papers.title: Broadband radio-frequency TEM specimen holders for in situ biasing excitation and 100-ps-scale electron beam control
papers.abstract: Broadband electrical excitation inside a transmission electron microscope (TEM) is required to investigate electrically driven nanodevices at their actual operating frequencies and to develop fully electrical time-resolved experiments at a sub-nanosecond range. Here, we report the performances of homemade two- and four-channel radio-frequency (RF) TEM specimen holders based on a hybrid architecture combining coaxial transmission lines with miniaturized impedance-controlled printed circuit boards (PCB). Removable mechanical contacts provide direct electrical connection to interchangeable TEM chips without wire bonding. Vector network analyzer measurements demonstrate broadband transmission through the complete electrical path up to the specimen. With a representative TEM chip, the two-channel holder exhibits a -3 dB bandwidth of 7.9 GHz, while insertion losses remain below 12 dB up to 18 GHz. The same RF holder architecture was used to drive a miniaturized electrostatic electron-beam deflector. The measured temporal response indicates that the holder deflector assembly remains compatible with electrical pulse durations approaching 100 ps, with the shortest accessible times presently limited by the available waveform generator. High-resolution TEM imaging with a 200 ps probe window does not show detectable degradation of spatial resolution, while off-axis electron holography is successfully performed for probe durations down to 0.5 ns under conditions representative of operando measurements. These results establish a versatile broadband platform combining GHz electrical excitation and sub-nanosecond electron-beam control. The dual-stage configuration of our Hitachi HF3300 microscope further provides the basis for a future fully electrical pump-probe TEM approach using independently driven RF holders for specimen excitation and electron-probe control.

papers.title: Plasmon Collapse in a Directional Strange Metal
papers.abstract: Strange metals are widespread in strongly correlated quantum matter and closely intertwined with high-temperature superconductivity and quantum criticality, yet their microscopic charge dynamics remain fundamentally unresolved. Whether well-defined collective modes survive in an incoherent electronic fluid or dissolve into overdamped continua remains intensely debated. Here, employing high-momentum-resolution inelastic electron scattering complemented by direction-resolved transport, we show that the van der Waals compound $\mathrm{MoOCl}_2$, a "bad" metal known to host unusually "good" plasmons, exhibits a striking dichotomy in electronic coherence and charge dynamics. Transport reveals coherent Fermi liquid behavior along one in-plane crystallographic axis and an incoherent strange metal response along the orthogonal axis. This dichotomy extends directly to the charge response. The Fermi liquid direction supports a well-defined, long-lived plasmon, whereas the strange metal direction exhibits an overdamped excitation that progressively loses its collective character with increasing momentum. Beyond a critical momentum ($q_c$ $\approx$ 0.008 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}^{-1}$), the mode undergoes a reversal into negative dispersion and ultimately collapses into a broad, nearly featureless continuum with a robust high-energy boundary ($E_c$ $\approx$ 1.75 eV). Remarkably, thickness-dependent measurements show that both $q_c$ and $E_c$ remain nearly unchanged despite substantial modifications of Coulomb screening, revealing them as intrinsic scales of incoherent charge density fluctuations. These results establish a unique single-material platform in which coherent and incoherent electronic states are partitioned into in-plane orthogonal channels, and demonstrate that incoherent electronic fluids retain intrinsically structured charge dynamics beyond the quasiparticle paradigm.

papers.title: Strain-enhanced superconductivity in RuO$_2$ thin films: Joint experimental and theoretical studies
papers.abstract: We investigate the superconducting properties of RuO$_2$ films grown on TiO$_2$ substrates by combining film fabrication and transport measurement with \textit{ab initio} calculation. Experimentally, we grow several RuO$_2$ (110) thin films on TiO$_2$ (110) substrates and observe superconductivity with critical temperature ($T_c$) of $\sim$2.0 K in 20-nm and 30-nm RuO$_2$ (110) thin films. Theoretically, we study the superconductivity in both RuO$_2$ (110) and RuO$_2$ (100) epitaxial films within McMillan formalism of isotropic Migdal-Eliashberg theory. Among the salient results, the calculated phonon dispersion relations of all the considered RuO$_2$ films show that the epitaxial films are dynamically stable. Importantly, our \textit{ab initio} calculations reveal that independent of the film orientation, the [001] compressive strain $ε_{[001]}$ pushes the flat Ru $d_{z^2}$-dominant bands towards the Fermi level ($E_F$), and significantly soften the out-of-plane acoustic phonon mode near the R point in the Brillouin zone, which substantially enhances the electron-phonon coupling (EPC) strength $λ$ and hence the calculated $T_c$ in the RuO$_2$ films. Remarkably, the amount of the phonon softening and the enhanced $T_c$ increase almost linearly with the increasing $ε_{[001]}$. The calculated $T_c$ for the films with thickness of $\geq$ 20 nm agree well with the experimental $T_c$. These findings demonstrate that among other things, lattice mismatch strain provides an effective route for tuning phonon-mediated superconductivity in RuO$_2$ and other thin films.

papers.title: Localized states of the non-Hermitian Schr{ö}dinger equation with a complex $1/r^{2}$ potential: from Efimov states to bipolarons
papers.abstract: We study the non-Hermitian Schrödinger equation with a complex $1/r^{2}$ potential, which bridges Hermitian few-body and non-Hermitian many-body physics: a real attractive potential describes Efimov bound states, whereas a purely imaginary one describes the medium-induced interaction between two heavy polarons at large separations. We solve this equation analytically, obtaining both the localized and continuum states, and compare the solutions with numerical and WKB results. As the imaginary part of the potential is increased, the energies of the Efimov bound states acquire imaginary parts and rotate counterclockwise in the complex plane. On approaching the purely imaginary potential, the excited states disappear sequentially, while the Efimov ground state is smoothly connected to a bipolaron state localized at short distance. Such a bipolaron is localized solely by the medium-induced imaginary interaction, without any attractive real potential. Solving the equation by finite differences, we find that each bipolaron state is necessarily accompanied by another localized state that oscillates on the scale of the mesh size and hence has no counterpart in the continuum limit. Each such pair coalesces at an exceptional point as the strength of the purely imaginary potential is varied, whereas the coalescence is lifted once a finite real part is introduced. We show that this behavior originates from a symmetry of the discretized Schrödinger equation that holds for any purely imaginary potential.

papers.title: Modified anisotropy and distinct phase diagrams in the nearly isotropic $S=1$ triangular-lattice antiferromagnet $\mathrm{Rb_2Ni(SeO_3)_2}$
papers.abstract: The triangular-lattice antiferromagnet serves as a benchmark platform for realizing exotic quantum phases, in which magnetic anisotropy plays an essential role. In this work, we report modified magnetic anisotropy and phase diagrams in the nearly isotropic $S=1$ triangular-lattice antiferromagnet $\mathrm{Rb_2Ni(SeO_3)_2}$, compared with those of its isostructural analog $\mathrm{K_2Ni(SeO_3)_2}$. The magnetic susceptibility of $\mathrm{Rb_2Ni(SeO_3)_2}$ exhibits an easy-axis anisotropy with $g_c > g_{ab}$, opposite to the easy-plane anisotropy observed in $\mathrm{K_2Ni(SeO_3)_2}$. The single Néel transition observed at zero field splits into two transitions at around 10~T, and a magnetization plateau is observed between 21~T and 37~T for both out-of-plane ($H\parallel c$) and in-plane ($H\parallel ab$) field directions in $\mathrm{Rb_2Ni(SeO_3)_2}$. We construct magnetic phase diagrams that are distinct between $\mathrm{Rb_2Ni(SeO_3)_2}$ and $\mathrm{K_2Ni(SeO_3)_2}$. These findings highlight the sensitivity of field-induced magnetic phase behavior to anisotropy in nearly isotropic triangular-lattice antiferromagnets.

papers.title: Discontinuous-Property Mechanical Metamaterials: A Framework for Discontinuous Lattice Dynamics
papers.abstract: Discontinuity, as the extreme limit of nonlinearity, is common in macroscopic continuum systems. This work introduces discontinuous-property mechanical metamaterials (DPMMs) as a prototype for establishing a geometric-mechanics framework for discontinuous lattice systems. We extend band theory to systems with complementary constraints through geometric regularization and analyze modal discontinuities. By analyzing its static, modal, and transient responses, we validated discontinuous stiffness and Poisson's ratio, alongside intense nonlinear wave mixing and mode conversion. A proof-of-concept experiment demonstrates the practical feasibility of implementing DPMMs. This work characterizes discontinuous lattice systems through the intuitive DPMM concept and provides a practical framework to harness sharp transitions in mechanical metamaterials for nonlinear wave manipulation.

papers.title: Large Language Model-Assisted Systematic Study of Anomalous Adsorption Phenomena
papers.abstract: Soft porous crystals can undergo guest-induced structural transitions producing unconventional adsorption isotherms, which are valuable for gas separation and storage applications. However, the evidence for these transitions is scattered across the literature in narrative form and has not been aggregated. Here we use a large language model pipeline to mine the literature for anomalous adsorption, extracting phase-transition events together with material, adsorbate, temperature and pressure metadata and classifying each into an established behavioural class. Benchmarked against human annotation, the extraction stage attains an F1 score of 0.96. When applied at scale, the pipeline yields a curated corpus of 547 transitions across 240 distinct materials, drawn from 200 of 4,252 screened publications, which we further link to crystallographic structures. Analysis of this database shows that the principal behavioural classes, gate-opening and breathing, are distinguished by their functional response. Gate-opening frameworks transform at a significantly lower pressure than breathing frameworks (p = 3.8E-3). In contrast, no difference in pore size, void fraction, linker chemistry or metal identity was detected between the classes. Our findings argue for a functional rather than purely structural description of responsive porous materials. They also highlight the need for a community database that records the guest, temperature and pressure of every reported transition of these materials.

papers.title: MASON: Materials Atomistic Structure builder Operated in Natural language
papers.abstract: Building reliable atomistic models is a critical and often challenging step in first-principles calculations. Although large language model agents can assist with structure generation, they lack direct capabilities for crystallographic operations and therefore struggle to construct complex structures reliably. Here we present MASON, an AI-native toolkit for atomistic structure construction that can be invoked by agents through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). In an end-to-end example, an agent builds a CO/Pt(111) adsorption model from a natural language request. By equipping agents with dedicated structure-building tools, MASON enables reliable and efficient atomistic model construction and provides a foundation for autonomous first-principles workflows.

papers.title: The Blume-Capel Model as a $φ^6$ Field Theory: A Monte Carlo and Flow Model Study
papers.abstract: We report Monte Carlo simulations of a continuous spin variant of the Blume-Capel model. We compute the phase diagrams in the crystal-field-temperature plane, as a function of the softness of the spins. We show that normalizing flows, a class of generative models capable of direct sampling without autocorrelation, are effective samplers across the phase diagram, including in the first-order transition region and in the vicinity of the tricritical point. Finite-size scaling analyses of flow samples locate the first- and second-order transitions as well as the tricritical point with accuracy comparable to canonical and extended-ensemble Monte Carlo.

papers.title: Fisher information analysis of a Langevin System with Thermal and Athermal Noise
papers.abstract: Fisher Information (FI) has proven to be a useful tool for estimating the parameters of a system when only statistical data are available. We apply this method to a system of Langevin equations analogous to the Brownian Gyrator, in which the coupling parameter $b$ and the athermal noise strength $D$ are treated as unknown quantities. Using the FI, we discuss the estimation of the coupling parameter between the degrees of freedom and the quantity $D$ associated with the external noise effects. We find that the diagonal components of the FI exhibit nontrivial behavior, whereas the off-diagonal components display a monotonic dependence on the parameters of interest. This distinction may contribute to an accurate estimation of $b$ and $D$.

papers.title: Denser-than-crystalline disordered polydisperse ellipse packings
papers.abstract: By employing SWAP Monte Carlo moves during slow Lubachevsky-Stillinger-like particle growth, we generate well-thermalized disordered jammed ellipse packings for a wide range of particle aspect ratios $α$ and maximum/minimum particle-diameter ratios $λ$. For $λ> λ_{\rm xtal}(α)$, the packings are denser than the perfect monodisperse ellipse crystal ($φ_{\rm xtal}^{\rm mono} = π/2\sqrt{3} \simeq 0.9069$) despite lacking any obvious long-range structural order; we find that $λ_{\rm xtal}(α)$ remains below $2.88$ over the range $1 \leq α\leq 5$, and drops below $1.65$ for $α\simeq 1.2$. These disordered $φ> φ_{\rm xtal}^{\rm mono}$ packings are the first of their kind reported for anisotropic particles. Multiscale analyses reveal that their characteristic structural motifs are strongly $α$- and $λ$-dependent, but none of the examined metrics change sharply as the $λ= λ_{\rm xtal}(α)$ boundary is crossed. For example, we find that packings with $α\simeq 1.2$ and $λ\simeq λ_{\rm xtal}(α)$ exhibit a fractionated-hexatic-plastic-polycrystalline structure that (like that of the recently-reported ideal disk glasses) can be exactly-isostatic, triangulated, and effectively-hyperuniform with respect to packing-fraction fluctuations. In contrast, even-denser packings with larger $α$ and $λ$ have none of these properties.

papers.title: One-way electron mirrors from single-layer stacking shifts in rhombohedral graphite
papers.abstract: One-way mirrors or asymmetric scatterers are key components of photonic systems, protecting sources from back-reflections and routing light along a chosen path. Acoustic systems can also be engineered to show asymmetric reflection. However, a condensed matter platform acting as a one-way mirror without breaking linearity, time-reversal symmetry or energy conservation has been lacking. One route to achieving this is mode selection, where a probe coupled to only some modes sees a boundary as a mirror from one side and as transparent from the other. Here we show that single-layer stacking shifts in six-layer rhombohedral graphite provide this platform, acting as one-way mirrors for electrons. In scanning tunneling microscopy, 10 nm scale interference fringes appear only on the stacking fault side of a wall, tracking its Dirac band, the rhombohedral side remaining transparent. Layer-resolved tight-binding and wave-packet dynamics calculations reproduce this and trace the asymmetry to the mismatched layer polarization across the wall, with the tip supplying the selective coupling. Because stacking solitons glide under external fields, this mirror forms a movable element of electron optics defined by the crystal structure alone.

证据与比较：扫描隧道显微镜中约10 nm尺度的干涉条纹仅出现在壁的堆垛层错一侧，并沿其狄拉克带（Dirac band）分布；层分辨紧束缚与波包动力学计算重现该现象，并将不对称性归因于跨壁层极化（layer polarization）失配。
papers.method_zh: 扫描隧道显微镜测量，以及层分辨紧束缚（tight-binding）计算和波包动力学（wave-packet dynamics）计算。

english_guide.finding: Single-layer stacking shifts in six-layer rhombohedral graphite act as one-way mirrors for electrons: 10 nm scale interference fringes appear only on the stacking-fault side of a wall, while the rhombohedral side remains transparent.
english_guide.question: Whether a condensed matter platform can act as a one-way mirror without breaking linearity, time-reversal symmetry or energy conservation, via mode selection in which a probe couples to only some modes.
english_guide.evidence: Scanning tunneling microscopy shows 10 nm scale interference fringes only on the stacking-fault side, tracking the Dirac band; layer-resolved tight-binding and wave-packet dynamics calculations reproduce this and trace the asymmetry to mismatched layer polarization across the wall.
english_guide.method: Scanning tunneling microscopy, layer-resolved tight-binding calculations and wave-packet dynamics calculations.
english_guide.novelty: The authors state that a condensed matter one-way mirror platform without breaking linearity, time-reversal symmetry or energy conservation has been lacking, and present the stacking-shift wall as this platform.
english_guide.limitations: The abstract covers only six-layer rhombohedral graphite under scanning tunneling microscopy, with the tip supplying selective coupling; applicability to other layer counts, temperatures or disorder is not stated.

papers.novelty_zh: 作者称此前缺乏不破坏线性、时间反演对称性或能量守恒的凝聚态单向镜平台，并称该堆垛位移壁提供了电子单向镜。
papers.limitations_zh: 摘要仅涉及六层菱方石墨与扫描隧道显微镜条件；探针提供选择性耦合，未说明其他层数、温度或无序条件下的适用性。

papers.title: Casimir Sign Reversal from Finite-Range Bogoliubov Fluctuations
papers.abstract: We study the zero-temperature Casimir effect of a three-dimensional Bose fluid with finite-range corrections to its Bogoliubov spectrum. Beyond the universal acoustic contribution scaling as $L^{-3}$, the long-distance expansion contains a nonuniversal $L^{-5}$ correction that can compete with the phononic term. We derive this crossover analytically within a minimal isotropic finite-range model and test the asymptotic result against the full dispersion. A regulator-independent Poisson-resummed calculation confirms that sign reversals of the Casimir energy are possible, while showing that the apparent low-coupling zero inferred by balancing only the $L^{-3}$ and $L^{-5}$ terms is not quantitatively controlled. Robust sign changes instead occur in the stable regime close to roton softening, where the Casimir energy acquires an oscillatory finite-momentum contribution. Strongly dipolar atomic gases provide a natural motivation for microscopic interaction lengths in the nanometric regime. We further discuss how the resulting nonlinear force law could be probed through the frequency response of a driven nanomechanical resonator.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：理论；基于解析推导与数值验证；研究对象：具有有限程Bogoliubov谱修正的三维Bose流体
papers.abstract_summary_zh: 有限程Bogoliubov涨落可导致Casimir能量符号反转，稳健反转出现在接近roton软化的稳定区。
papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：有限程修正如何影响三维Bose流体零温Casimir效应，以及符号反转在何种条件下发生？
证据与比较：解析推导出L^{-5}非普适修正与声学项竞争；用完整色散检验渐近结果；Poisson重求和计算确认符号反转，并表明仅平衡L^{-3}与L^{-5}项得到的低耦合零点不受定量控制。
papers.method_zh: 最小各向同性有限程模型解析推导；与完整色散对比；调节子无关的Poisson重求和计算。

english_guide.finding: Finite-range Bogoliubov fluctuations can reverse the sign of the Casimir energy, with robust reversals occurring in the stable regime close to roton softening.
english_guide.question: How do finite-range corrections to the Bogoliubov spectrum affect the zero-temperature Casimir effect of a three-dimensional Bose fluid, and under what conditions does sign reversal occur?
english_guide.evidence: Analytic derivation of a nonuniversal L^{-5} correction competing with the acoustic term; asymptotic result tested against the full dispersion; regulator-independent Poisson-resummed calculation confirms sign reversals and shows the apparent low-coupling zero from balancing only L^{-3} and L^{-5} terms is not quantitatively controlled.
english_guide.method: Analytic derivation within a minimal isotropic finite-range model; comparison with full dispersion; regulator-independent Poisson-resummed calculation.
english_guide.novelty: Authors claim that finite-range Bogoliubov fluctuations can produce sign reversals of the Casimir energy, with robust reversals in the stable regime close to roton softening.
english_guide.limitations: Abstract does not specify material parameters, temperature corrections, or experimental feasibility; strongly dipolar gases serve as motivation and nanomechanical probing is discussed as a proposal.

papers.novelty_zh: 作者声称：有限程Bogoliubov涨落可导致Casimir能量符号反转，且稳健反转出现在接近roton软化的稳定区。
papers.limitations_zh: 摘要未明确说明具体材料参数、温度修正及实验可行性；强偶极气体仅作为动机，纳米机械探测为讨论性建议。

papers.title: Material dependence of direct light-induced charge injection from metallic nanoparticles into adsorbates
papers.abstract: Direct injection of charge from metallic nanoparticles into adsorbed molecules via the chemical interface damping of localized surface plasmons has emerged as a promising avenue to avoid the rapid thermalization of hot carriers. In this paper, we develop an approach for predicting hot-electron and hot-hole injection rates from large spherical nanoparticles into adsorbed carbon monoxide (CO) molecules. The approach combines a detailed description of the adsorbate-metal interactions via ab initio density functional theory with a macroscopic electrodynamics treatment of the localized surface plasmon. We apply this approach to nine different metals including both traditional (Ag, Au, Cu) and emerging (Al) plasmonic metals as well as non-plasmonic metals (Ni, Rh, Pd, Ir, Pt). For all metals, hot-electron injection is larger than hot-hole injection. This is a consequence of the alignment of the CO frontier orbitals, with the CO lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) being closer to the metal Fermi energy than the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO). The largest electron injection rates in the optical photon ranges are obtained for Al, Ag, Cu and Au, with Cu and Au showing significant plasmonic enhancement. The non-plasmonic metals show weak electron injection as a consequence of their high LUMO energies relative to the metal Fermi level. The results of our study pave the way towards a rational design of metallic nanoscale photocatalysts for specific chemical processes.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：计算研究；结合第一性原理DFT与宏观电动力学建模；研究对象：九种金属（Ag、Au、Cu、Al、Ni、Rh、Pd、Ir、Pt）球形纳米颗粒与吸附CO分子体系
papers.abstract_summary_zh: 所有金属中热电子注入均强于热空穴注入，源于CO的LUMO比HOMO更靠近金属费米能级；光频段电子注入率以Al、Ag、Cu、Au最大，其中Cu和Au表现出显著的等离激元增强。
papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：如何预测大尺寸球形金属纳米颗粒向吸附CO分子直接注入热电子与热空穴的速率，并考察其材料依赖性？
证据与比较：对九种金属计算了热电子与热空穴注入速率；所有金属均显示电子注入大于空穴注入，归因于CO前线轨道相对金属费米能级的排列；光频段最大电子注入率出现在Al、Ag、Cu、Au，Cu与Au有显著等离激元增强；非等离激元金属因LUMO相对费米能级偏高而注入较弱。
papers.method_zh: 用从头算密度泛函理论描述吸附物-金属相互作用，结合局域表面等离激元的宏观电动力学处理，预测大球形纳米颗粒的注入速率。

english_guide.finding: For all nine metals, hot-electron injection exceeds hot-hole injection because the CO LUMO lies closer to the metal Fermi energy than the HOMO; the largest optical-range electron injection rates occur for Al, Ag, Cu and Au, with Cu and Au showing significant plasmonic enhancement, while non-plasmonic metals show weak injection due to high LUMO energies relative to the Fermi level.
english_guide.question: How can hot-electron and hot-hole injection rates from large spherical metallic nanoparticles into adsorbed CO molecules be predicted, and how do they depend on the metal?
english_guide.evidence: Calculated hot-electron and hot-hole injection rates for nine metals; electron injection exceeds hole injection for all metals, attributed to CO frontier orbital alignment relative to the metal Fermi energy; largest optical-range electron injection for Al, Ag, Cu and Au, with significant plasmonic enhancement for Cu and Au; weak injection for non-plasmonic metals due to high LUMO energies relative to the Fermi level.
english_guide.method: Combines ab initio density functional theory for adsorbate-metal interactions with a macroscopic electrodynamics treatment of the localized surface plasmon to predict injection rates from large spherical nanoparticles.
english_guide.novelty: The authors state they develop an approach for predicting hot-electron and hot-hole injection rates from large spherical nanoparticles into adsorbed CO molecules and apply it to nine metals.
english_guide.limitations: The abstract does not specify nanoparticle size range or CO coverage conditions; results are based on a computational model, and the abstract provides no experimental validation.

papers.novelty_zh: 作者称建立了预测大球形纳米颗粒向吸附CO分子注入热电子与热空穴速率的方法，并系统比较九种金属。

papers.title: Sb-5$p$-mediated antiparallel Nd-Fe coupling in Nd$_3$Fe$_3$Sb$_7$
papers.abstract: We uncover the microscopic mechanism underlying the antiparallel Nd-Fe coupling in the intermetallic 4$f$-3$d$-5$p$ compound Nd$_3$Fe$_3$Sb$_7$ by means of high-field x-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) spectroscopy, complemented by magnetization measurements and density-functional-theory (DFT) calculations. This coupling is unexpected for intermetallics composed of light rare-earth and transition-metal elements. Sb $M_{4,5}$-edge XMCD measurements indicate a clear spin polarization of Sb 5$p$ states antiparallel to the Fe 3$d$ moments. DFT calculations reveal the site-dependent character of the Sb moments and, together with the Fe-Sb antiparallel alignment seen by XMCD, identify a Fe 3$d$-Sb 5$p$-Nd 5$d$ hybridization pathway for the antiparallel Nd-Fe coupling. Pulsed-field XMCD reveals a field-induced spin reorientation through the evolution of the $c$-axis projections of the Nd and Fe moments. Nd$_3$Fe$_3$Sb$_7$, thus, provides a platform for exploring antiparallel rare-earth-transition-metal ($R$-$T$) coupling mediated by transition-metal 3$d$-ligand $p$-rare-earth 5$d$ hybridization in light-$R$-$T$ intermetallics with $p$-elements.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：实验与计算结合；高场XMCD谱、磁化测量加DFT计算；研究对象：金属间化合物Nd3Fe3Sb7（4f-3d-5p体系）
papers.abstract_summary_zh: Nd3Fe3Sb7中Nd-Fe反平行耦合由Fe 3d-Sb 5p-Nd 5d杂化路径介导，Sb 5p自旋极化与Fe 3d磁矩反平行。
papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：轻稀土-过渡金属金属间化合物中通常不预期的Nd-Fe反平行耦合，其微观机制是什么。
证据与比较：Sb M4,5边XMCD显示Sb 5p自旋极化与Fe 3d磁矩反平行；DFT给出Sb磁矩的位点依赖特征；脉冲强场XMCD显示Nd与Fe磁矩c轴投影随场演化，指示场致自旋重取向。
papers.method_zh: 高场X射线磁圆二色（XMCD）谱、磁化测量、脉冲强场XMCD，以及密度泛函理论（DFT）计算。

english_guide.finding: Sb 5p states are spin-polarized antiparallel to Fe 3d moments, and a Fe 3d-Sb 5p-Nd 5d hybridization pathway mediates the antiparallel Nd-Fe coupling in Nd3Fe3Sb7.
english_guide.question: What is the microscopic mechanism of the unexpected antiparallel Nd-Fe coupling in the light rare-earth-transition-metal intermetallic Nd3Fe3Sb7?
english_guide.evidence: Sb M4,5-edge XMCD indicates Sb 5p spin polarization antiparallel to Fe 3d moments; DFT reveals site-dependent Sb moments; pulsed-field XMCD shows field-induced spin reorientation via c-axis projections of Nd and Fe moments.
english_guide.method: High-field x-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) spectroscopy, magnetization measurements, pulsed-field XMCD, and density-functional-theory (DFT) calculations.
english_guide.novelty: The authors claim to uncover the microscopic mechanism and identify a Fe 3d-Sb 5p-Nd 5d hybridization pathway for the antiparallel Nd-Fe coupling.
english_guide.limitations: Abstract does not specify sample conditions, measurement temperatures, or quantitative uncertainties; RSS excerpt may be truncated and full text was not read.

papers.limitations_zh: 摘要未明确说明样品条件、测量温区与定量误差；RSS片段可能截断，未读全文。

papers.title: Grain-Size Dependence of Thermal and Electrical Properties in (Cr,Mo,Ta,V,W)C1-δ High-Entropy Carbide Ceramics
papers.abstract: Thermal and electrical transport in high-entropy carbides can be influenced by grain-boundary scattering, but the relevant microstructural regime remains uncertain. Here, near-fully dense $(Cr,Mo,Ta,V,W)C_{1-δ}$ ceramics were densified by spark plasma sintering at 1750-1950 °C, producing average grain sizes from 9.3 $\pm$ 4.9 to 28.8 $\pm$ 15.3 $μ$m while retaining the rock-salt phase. Heat capacities were measured experimentally and estimated by the Neumann-Kopp law with the latter used to calculate thermal conductivity. Thermal conductivity values were in the range of 6.8-7.1 W $m^{-1}$ $K^{-1}$ at room temperature, but showed no systematic dependence on grain size within the investigated range. Room-temperature electrical resistivity values were in the range of 151.9 to 177.0 $μΩ$ cm and likewise showed no grain-size dependence. The electron contribution to room-temperature thermal conductivity was estimated to be approximately 58-68% of total thermal conductivity as estimated using the Wiedemann-Franz law and the theoretical Lorenz number. The results indicated that processing-induced grain coarsening did not produce clearly resolvable transport-property changes under the conditions investigated leading to the conclusion that intrinsic disorder and defect chemistry may exert stronger influences on properties.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：实验；SPS烧结陶瓷并测热容、热导与电阻率；研究对象：(Cr,Mo,Ta,V,W)C1-δ高熵碳化物陶瓷，岩盐相，平均晶粒9.3–28.8 μm
papers.abstract_summary_zh: 在所研究晶粒尺寸范围内，热导率与电阻率均未呈现可分辨的晶粒尺寸依赖，作者据此认为本征无序与缺陷化学可能影响更强。
papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：高熵碳化物的热与电输运受晶界散射影响，但相关微观结构区间尚不明确；本文考察加工引起的晶粒粗化是否改变输运性质。
证据与比较：室温热导率6.8–7.1 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹，电阻率151.9–177.0 μΩ cm，均无系统晶粒尺寸依赖；用Wiedemann-Franz定律与理论Lorenz数估算电子贡献约占总热导58–68%。
papers.method_zh: 放电等离子烧结（SPS）于1750–1950 °C致密化；热容实验测量并以Neumann-Kopp定律估算，后者用于计算热导率。

english_guide.finding: Thermal conductivity was 6.8-7.1 W m^-1 K^-1 and electrical resistivity 151.9-177.0 μΩ cm at room temperature, with no systematic grain-size dependence; the electron contribution was estimated at approximately 58-68% of total thermal conductivity.
english_guide.question: Grain-boundary scattering can influence thermal and electrical transport in high-entropy carbides, but the relevant microstructural regime remains uncertain; whether processing-induced grain coarsening changes transport properties was examined.
english_guide.evidence: Near-fully dense (Cr,Mo,Ta,V,W)C1-δ ceramics were densified by spark plasma sintering at 1750-1950 °C, giving average grain sizes from 9.3 ± 4.9 to 28.8 ± 15.3 μm while retaining the rock-salt phase; heat capacities were measured experimentally and estimated by the Neumann-Kopp law, the latter used to calculate thermal conductivity; the electron contribution was estimated using the Wiedemann-Franz law and the theoretical Lorenz number.
english_guide.method: Spark plasma sintering at 1750-1950 °C; experimental heat capacity measurement and Neumann-Kopp law estimation; thermal conductivity calculation; Wiedemann-Franz law with theoretical Lorenz number.
english_guide.novelty: The authors do not explicitly claim novelty in the abstract; they report that processing-induced grain coarsening did not produce clearly resolvable transport-property changes under the conditions investigated.
english_guide.limitations: The conclusion is limited to near-fully dense, rock-salt-phase samples with grain sizes of 9.3-28.8 μm and the measured temperature; the abstract does not address finer grains, other temperatures, or compositional fluctuations.

papers.title: Transition-Metal-Oxygen Covalency Controls Ligand-Hole Stability in Li-Rich Cathode
papers.abstract: Lithium-rich cathodes boast a large specific capacity due to the presence of excess lithium per transition metal. However, making use of that excess Li drives the cathodes to unusually high formal oxidation states, often triggering unwanted side reactions, typically signaled by gas release and commonly associated with oxygen oxidation. By varying the transition metal (TM) chemistry in Li-rich materials, cyclability can vary drastically, with some materials suffering rapid capacity fade while others are able to maintain large and stable voltage windows. Such observations indicate a crucial role for both TM and O activities, but the details remain elusive. Here, we model core-level spectroscopy to understand differences in the charge compensation mechanism between different Li2MO3 (M = Mn, Ru, Ir) cathode materials. We find that ligand holes are important throughout the series, but their stability depends strongly on the transition-metal-oxygen electronic structure. In Li2MnO3, the ground state is already strongly negative-charge-transfer-like, so further delithiation rapidly increases ligand-hole character and promotes instability. Moving from Mn to Ru and Ir increases TM-O hybridization while reducing the tendency toward an extreme negative-charge-transfer state, allowing additional holes to remain delocalized over the covalent TM-O network over a wider range of charge. These results identify TM-O covalency, rather than the absence of oxygen-hole character, as a key factor controlling reversible high-valent redox and suggest a route for stabilizing high-energy-density cathodes without invoking reversible molecular oxygen formation.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：计算：用核心能级谱建模比较三种材料；研究对象：富锂正极材料 Li2MO3（M = Mn、Ru、Ir）
papers.abstract_summary_zh: 配体空穴在整个 Li2MO3 系列中都存在，但其稳定性由过渡金属-氧共价性（TM-O covalency）决定，而非取决于是否出现氧空穴特征。
papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：为何不同过渡金属的富锂材料循环性能差异巨大，TM 与 O 的电荷补偿机制有何不同。
证据与比较：摘要称 Li2MnO3 基态已呈强负电荷转移（negative-charge-transfer）特征，脱锂会迅速增强配体空穴特征；由 Mn 到 Ru、Ir，TM-O 杂化增强、趋向极端负电荷转移态的趋势减弱，空穴可在更宽电荷范围内离域于共价 TM-O 网络。
papers.method_zh: 对 Li2MO3（M = Mn、Ru、Ir）建模核心能级谱（core-level spectroscopy），比较电荷补偿机制。

english_guide.finding: Ligand holes exist across the Li2MO3 series, but their stability is governed by TM-O covalency rather than by the presence or absence of oxygen-hole character.
english_guide.question: Why do Li-rich cathodes with different transition metals differ so strongly in cyclability, and how do TM and O charge compensation mechanisms differ?
english_guide.evidence: The abstract reports that Li2MnO3 has a strongly negative-charge-transfer-like ground state, with delithiation rapidly increasing ligand-hole character; moving from Mn to Ru and Ir enhances TM-O hybridization and reduces the tendency toward an extreme negative-charge-transfer state, allowing holes to remain delocalized over the covalent TM-O network over a wider charge range.
english_guide.method: Core-level spectroscopy modeling of Li2MO3 (M = Mn, Ru, Ir) to compare charge compensation mechanisms.
english_guide.novelty: The authors identify TM-O covalency, rather than the absence of oxygen-hole character, as a key factor controlling reversible high-valent redox.
english_guide.limitations: The abstract does not specify computational parameters, voltage windows, or experimental validation; the RSS snippet may be truncated and the full text was not read.

papers.title: Identifying intercalation electrodes for electrochemical ion recovery and desalination
papers.abstract: Water sources serve as a requirement for human consumption, industrial, and agricultural needs and a resource for valuable ions. Appropriate treatment of water that captures ions from the aqueous solution can give rise to suitable `products', such as critical ions (such as Li$^+$) in selective ion recovery and usable water in the case of desalination (i.e., removal of non-essential ions). Among myriad ion capture techniques, we focus on electrochemical methods using intercalation electrodes, an energy-efficient approach capable of both selectively extracting specific ions or non-selectively extracting multiple ions from diverse water sources. However, practical realization of electrochemical ion capture requires the use of robust cation intercalation electrodes, with the state-of-the-art olivine-FePO$_4$ and spinel-Mn$_2$O$_4$ exhibiting several shortcomings. Thus, we develop a high-throughput computational workflow to identify potential intercalation electrodes for both ion recovery and desalination from a pool of 20,414 Li, Mg, Ca, Na, and/or K-containing structures from the Materials Project database. Based on the construction of Pourbaix diagrams relevant for electrodes operating under seawater conditions, modifying criteria used for defining metastability in seawater, computing average intercalation voltages and the extent of metastability of electrode structures, and computational graphs to encode ionic selectivity, we identify a total of 11 promising electrodes for selective ion recovery and one possible desalination electrode. The promising materials identified in this work include Fe$_2$(MoO$_4$)$_3$, Li$_3$Fe$_2$(PO$_4$)$_3$, LiFeP$_2$O$_7$ for selective Li-recovery. Our study provides thermodynamic insights, qualitative trends, and a promising list of intercalation electrodes for experimental testing that should advance the field of electrochemical ion recovery.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：计算；基于Materials Project数据库的高通量DFT筛选；研究对象：含Li、Mg、Ca、Na和/或K的20,414种结构，用于电化学离子回收与脱盐的插层电极
papers.abstract_summary_zh: 从20,414种结构中筛选出11种有前景的选择性离子回收电极和1种可能的脱盐电极，包括Fe2(MoO4)3、Li3Fe2(PO4)3、LiFeP2O7用于选择性Li回收。
papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：如何从大规模材料数据库中识别出在海水条件下稳定、具有合适插层电压和离子选择性的稳健阳离子插层电极，以替代存在缺点的橄榄石-FePO4和尖晶石-Mn2O4？

papers.title: Modeling Transport and Mechanics in Anion Exchange Membranes to Optimize Continuous CO2 Separations
papers.abstract: Water transport in charged polymer membranes is strongly influenced by hydration-dependent transport properties and polymer-network deformation. Under water-activity gradients, spatial variations in water concentration induce swelling and mechanical stresses, while the resulting deformation can influence water transport. Capturing this bidirectional interaction is important for predicting membrane behavior under nonuniform hydration conditions. This study develops a transient finite element model of water transport and mechanical deformation in a Fumasep FAA-3-50 anion exchange membrane. The framework incorporates concentration-dependent water diffusivity, hygroscopic swelling, and nonlinear viscoelastic polymer response. Uncoupled, one-way coupled, and fully coupled formulations are compared to distinguish the effects of hydration-dependent diffusivity and mechanical coupling. In the fully coupled model, local water concentration governs swelling and mechanical response, while deformation, evolving membrane geometry, and mechanical pressure feed back into water transport. Simulations predict spatially and temporally nonuniform swelling and deformation that track the evolving water-concentration field. Relative to the uncoupled concentration-dependent diffusion model, mechanical feedback alters the predicted transport response, although transport remains primarily diffusion-driven. The fully coupled model is validated against steady-state water-transport measurements across water-activity gradients and reproduces the experimentally observed hydration dependence, with strongest agreement at intermediate hydration levels. These results highlight the importance of coupled hydration, swelling, deformation, and transport processes in models of hydrated anion exchange membranes and provide a framework for evaluating membrane behavior in moisture-facilitated transport applications.

papers.title: Enabling large language model agents for high-fidelity many-body perturbation theory calculations
papers.abstract: Many-body perturbation theory (MBPT) methods, including the GW approximation, the GW plus Bethe-Salpeter equation (GW-BSE) method, and GW perturbation theory (GWPT), among others, provide accurate first-principles descriptions of excited-state properties and multiparticle interactions of materials. However, their use remains limited due to complex multi-software workflows, interdependent physical parameters, and substantial theoretical expertise. Large language model (LLM) agents, which couple a language model to software tools, show potential in automating computational tasks, but MBPT remains an unaddressed challenge. We show that LLM agents tested in our work, including frontier models such as Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5, do not reliably construct MBPT workflows in one attempt, suggesting that correct setup requires expert knowledge and consistency that current models lack. Across tested model-harness combinations, out-of-the-box agents average 54%, 36%, and 19% on GW, GW-BSE, and GWPT workflow benchmarks, with strong model dependence and large run-to-run variation. Errors typically originate from cross-stage inconsistencies that surface only several stages after they are introduced. We therefore develop AI-Donkey, an agentic framework that combines expert-curated knowledge with deterministic execution to enable high-fidelity GW, GW-BSE, and GWPT calculations and analyses. With AI-Donkey, all tested agents, from frontier proprietary models to open-weight models, produce complete, runnable MBPT workflows with no observed run-to-run variation. We further demonstrate autonomous calculations and post-processing on 1D, 2D, and bulk materials, including the many-body enhancement of Fröhlich electron-phonon coupling in polar semiconductors. Our approach provides a general framework for knowledge engineering to enable reliable agentic workflows in computational materials science.

papers.title: Resonant enhancement of Raman scattering in a MoS$_2$ nanotube
papers.abstract: The whispering-gallery modes confined in the wall of a multiwall MoS$_2$ nanotube resonantly enhance the spontaneous Raman scattering by its own optical phonons. The enhancement is doubly resonant --- pump and Stokes waves hit two adjacent modes at one pump energy, and the signal scales as $(Q_{\rm pump}Q_{\rm sc})^2$ - whenever a phonon energy matches the free spectral range of the mode ladder. Near the A exciton the excitonic dispersion compresses the ladder and sweeps its spacing through all intralayer phonon energies of MoS$_2$, so the match, reached for $A_{1g}$ at $E_{\rm pump}=1551$~meV, requires no geometric tuning. A missed match splits the excitation peak into a pump- and a scattered-resonant doublet whose splitting measures the residual detuning. Selection rules confine the double resonance to the TM$\to$TM channel and exclude $E_{1g}$.

papers.title: Quantum oscillations in a solvable model of a Kondo insulator
papers.abstract: We study the effects of interactions on the low-energy density of states (SdH) and magnetization (dHvA) quantum oscillations (QOs) in a Kondo insulator. Toward this end we introduce a generalization of the periodic Anderson model with Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) interactions at each site that is exactly solvable in the large-$N$ limit, where $N$ is the number of flavors of the heavy $f$ electrons. We show analytically and numerically that the insulating state remains stable in terms of spectrum, thermodynamics, and transport at low temperatures even for interaction strengths much larger than non-interacting band gap of the hybridization-gap insulator. We analytically derive generalizations of Lifshitz-Kosevich (LK) formulae, distinct for the SdH and dHvA QOs, for the interacting insulator. We find that the SdH oscillation frequencies, $F_0\pm δF$, corresponding to the conduction and valence band edges, can be weakly renormalized by interaction relative to their non-interacting values. In contrast, dHvA QO frequency $F_0$ is not renormalized by interactions, and remains the same as that for the non-interacting unhybridized bands. The QO amplitudes show a remarkable difference: the dHvA amplitude is essentially unaffected by interactions, while the SdH amplitude is strongly enhanced due to gap renormalization.

papers.title: Long-lived local coherences at high temperature from frozen domain walls
papers.abstract: Local coherences between distinct charge sectors--measured by the single-particle Green's function or the transverse spin autocorrelation function--do not overlap with hydrodynamic modes. At finite temperature, therefore, they decay faster than any power law in generic chaotic systems. We present a mechanism by which these coherences can persist anomalously long, for integrable and chaotic spin chains (including the XXZ and Fredkin spin chains) that obey a quantum group symmetry. We show--using a Mazur bound derived from the quantum-group symmetry, together with locality and a "non-undershoot" assumption--that the transverse spin autocorrelation function $C(t) \equiv \langle σ^-_x(t) σ^+_x(0)\rangle$ can decay at most algebraically: $C(t) \gtrsim 1/t^2$. This bound is not tight: in the large-anisotropy limit of the XXZ spin chain, at infinite temperature, we explicitly compute $C(t) \sim \sqrt{3}/(18 \sqrt{t})$. We also compute this decay rate in the XXZ spin chain for general easy-axis anisotropy, and estimate it to scale as $C(t) \sim t^{-2/z}$ (for transport exponent $z$) in the chaotic models.

papers.title: Boundary-induced geometrical frustration in a square Rydberg-atom lattice
papers.abstract: We study geometric defects in square-lattice Rydberg-atom arrays induced by lattice-size parity in the striated density-wave phase. While odd-sized lattices select a single striated domain, even-sized lattices seed incompatible domains at the four corners, resulting in a π/2-rotation invariant state with a geometrical defect emanating from the lattice center. At larger detunings, we instead identify a π-rotation-invariant state with two domains nucleated by opposite corners and separated by a one-dimensional diagonal defect. We probe the state-preparation protocol on the Aquila atomic quantum processor and benchmark it with equilibrium and real-time dynamics tensor-network simulations. Our results assess the role of boundaries and lattice size in determining the global ordering in programmable quantum matter.

papers.title: All-temperature superfluidity in two dimensions
papers.abstract: In local theories with short-range interactions, continuous symmetries cannot be spontaneously broken in two spatial dimensions at nonzero temperature. $\mathrm{U}(1)$-symmetric models instead admit a Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless (BKT) phase with quasi-long-range order and nonzero phase stiffness, which is normally destroyed at high temperatures by vortex proliferation. Here, we show that a BKT phase, and with it superfluidity, can persist to arbitrarily high temperatures. Using the large-$N$ expansion, we study a $(2+1)$-dimensional quantum field theory in which a complex scalar is coupled to the critical $\mathrm{O}(N)$ model. At the biconical fixed point, where the inter-sector coupling is negative, the thermal effective potential has a circle of minima with nonzero $\mathrm{U}(1)$ amplitude. Integrating out the gapped fluctuations yields an effective theory for the compact phase mode at distances large compared to $1/T$. Since temperature is the only scale at the fixed point, the phase stiffness grows linearly with temperature, with a proportionality factor that scales linearly with $N$ and is fixed entirely by the fixed point. This renders vortex operators irrelevant for sufficiently large $N$. We further show that the vortex fugacity is exponentially small in $N$.

papers.title: Transport in multilayer graphene: resistance from stacking faults
papers.abstract: Multilayer graphene exhibits rich possibilities for stacking. While natural bulk graphite predominantly occurs in the Bernal structure, where layers are stacked in an $-ABAB-$ pattern, rhombohedral stacking has sprung to prominence recently. It is well known that Bernal graphite exhibits anisotropic transport, with high resistance to currents along the stacking axis. Careful experiments using pillar geometries have measured out-of-plane resistance, attributing it to stacking faults where planes slip out of the nominal $ABAB$ sequence. The observed resistance shows anomalously large, non-Gaussian, sample-to-sample variations. In this article, we build a theoretical framework to calculate $c$-axis resistance of graphene stacks with an arbitrary stacking arrangement. Our approach builds on the idea that, regardless of stacking sequence, we have in-plane translational symmetry. With in-plane momentum as a good quantum number, $c$-axis transport reduces to an effectively one-dimensional problem that can be addressed using the Landauer paradigm. We calculate the resistances of a variety of simple stacking faults in both Bernal and rhombohedral systems. We also calculate the resistance of a rhombohedral 'slab' embedded between Bernal leads. Remarkably, despite both Bernal and rhombohedral graphite being metallic, the system exhibits insulating behaviour. We attribute this to Fermi surface mismatch. We next calculate the resistance of a multilayer sample with stacking disorder. Resistance is non-self-averaging, akin to a one-dimensional wire where disorder has a strong localizing effect. The median resistance grows exponentially with stack size, indicating insulating character driven by localization. Our results demonstrate that transport measurements on mesoscopic graphitic pillars serve as signatures of stacking faults, and in particular, probe localization-driven physics.

papers.title: Gyrators for superconducting circuit design
papers.abstract: Assuming only the solubility of Kirchhoff's laws, the conservation of energy, and the form of the constitutive relations, we present a flux-charge symmetric Hamiltonian formalism that always admits a symplectic reduction for nonsingular, well-posed circuits involving gyrators, inductors, and capacitors (LCG circuits) with arbitrary non-linearity. The formalism introduces a notion of circuit duality on non-linear non-reciprocal circuits and a family of point transformations that inserts, removes, and moves reciprocal elements across gyrators while preserving the Hamiltonian spectrum. With these transformations, we extend Tellegen's classic result that gyrators make reciprocal elements behave as their dual to non-linear reciprocal elements such as the Josephson junction and quantum phase slip. Furthermore, we present conditions under which non-reciprocal circuits can be transformed to dynamically equivalent reciprocal circuits.

papers.title: Operator-Space Entanglement Entropy in Random Fermionic Gaussian Dynamics
papers.abstract: We study the von Neumann operator-space entanglement entropy (OSEE) of initial product operators evolved under random gaussian dynamics, as modeled by a Brownian SYK$_2$ model. By exploiting a mapping to a domain-wall melting problem, we derive an exact expression for the time-dependent bipartite OSEE in the thermodynamic limit, and obtain an analytic characterization of the corresponding gaussian Page curve emerging at late times. Our results build on recent work on the entanglement dynamics in the all-to-all quantum simple exclusion process, leveraging tools from RMT, including the Coulomb-gas approach and a mapping to the free Jacobi process. Finally, based on our results, we discuss the possibility of relating the OSEE with non-gaussianity measures in the Heisenberg picture.

papers.title: Quantum instanton approach to metastable collective spin systems: Numerical implementation and applications
papers.abstract: Driven-dissipative collective spin systems can host several long-lived metastable states; rare switching between them governs slow relaxation and first-order dissipative phase transitions associated with changes in the dominant stationary state. In the companion Letter [arXiv:2604.15091], we introduced a quantum instanton framework based on exact quasiprobability dynamics to describe this switching and illustrated it with a minimal model possessing a simplifying symmetry. Here we develop its numerical implementation, combining collocation and shooting methods, and apply it to two microscopically motivated systems: the Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick model with purely collective dissipation and the cooperative resonance fluorescence with collective and local dissipation. By determining the leading exponential scaling of switching rates between metastable attractors, we predict the stationary magnetization, the first-order dissipative phase-transition point, and the exponential scaling of slow relaxation rates. These predictions agree with quantum master-equation calculations and an exact analytical result for the second model without dephasing. We also examine how the choice of quasiprobability representation affects numerical convergence and find that the alternative semiclassical Wigner approach, based on Gaussian truncation, has varying accuracy across models and parameter regimes. These results substantiate the framework's applicability to experimentally relevant collective spin systems with both collective and local dissipation.

papers.title: Difference between pair creation and anomaly matching: Nontrivial aspects of invertible symmetries and defects in $SU(N)$ models
papers.abstract: We study the connection between the $SU(N)_{K}$ Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW) model and $SU(N)_{K'}$ WZW models, enforcing the unbroken $\mathbb{Z}_{N}$ symmetries. The fundamental underlying structures are the (half-)integer spin simple currents in the topological quantum field theories and anomaly matching conditions in conformal field theories. For the (half-)integer spin simple current condition of the folded models $SU(N)_{K}\boxtimes_{\mathbb{Z}_{N}} \overline{SU(N)_{K'}}$ or $SU(N)_{K}\boxtimes_{\mathbb{Z}_{N}} SU(N)_{K'}$, we obtain the generalized pairing condition $K= \pm R^{2}K' (\text{mod}.N)$ with $\text{gcd}(R,N)=1$. On the other hand, the anomaly matching condition results in the weaker condition $K= \pm RUK' (\text{mod}.N)$ with $\text{gcd}(R,N)=\text{gcd}(U,N)=1$. Surprisingly, the anomaly matching without the pairing condition results in the intrinsic mismatch of the preservation law of the $\mathbb{Z}_{N}$ defects and symmetries. The pairing condition canonically relates symmetries and defects, as in category theory, whereas it is unclear whether it can be a guiding principle in prohibiting the massless renormalization group flows.

papers.title: Casimir forces on suspended thin dielectric membranes covered with graphene
papers.abstract: We investigate the Casimir force on thin suspended dielectric layers covered with graphene, both theoretically and experimentally. Thermal effects of the Casimir force on graphene occur at separations significantly smaller compared to ordinary metals and dielectrics. At such small separations, the Casimir force is sufficiently strong to be measured experimentally. However, the presence of substrates to support the graphene significantly reduces the enhancement. We show theoretically that replacing the solid substrate beneath graphene with a thin dielectric membrane partially restores this strong thermal dependence. One of the interacting objects is a solid gold plate. The other object is a suspended dielectric membrane made of either 15 nm of silicon oxide or 13 nm silicon nitride, covered with graphene. At a separation of $\sim$500 nm, theoretical predictions yield changes in the Casimir pressure of up to 54 % and 40 % for silicon oxide and silicon nitride, respectively, when the temperature is increased from 10 K to 294 K. Measurements were performed for graphene on a suspended silicon nitride membrane at room temperature, using a gold-coated sphere attached to a cantilever as the force sensor. The measured force gradient is consistent with the theoretical prediction, although the thermal dependence could not be resolved, in part because of uncertainties in the optical properties of silicon nitride. Replacing a bulk substrate with a thin dielectric membrane covered with graphene provides a substantial reduction of the Casimir force, which may facilitate the stable operation of neutral nanomechanical elements at small separations.

papers.title: Vision-Guided Closed-Loop Autonomous Navigation of Light-Driven Janus Microbots
papers.abstract: Artificial microbots capable of precise and autonomous navigation could provide versatile platforms for microscale transport, manipulation, and task execution in complex environments. However, reliable navigation becomes increasingly challenging at the micrometre scale, particularly when the surrounding environment changes dynamically. Here, we develop a vision-guided closed-loop navigation framework for light-driven cube-shaped hematite/TiO2 Janus microbots with a characteristic size of approximately 3 μm. Real-time visual localization using a custom-trained YOLOv11 object-detection model is integrated with discretized waypoint-based magnetic steering to enable precise navigation along complex prescribed trajectories, with more than 90% of the measured trajectory deviations remaining below 6 μm across the tested path geometries. The framework further enables arbitrary user-defined free-hand trajectories and autonomous navigation through a physically confined maze. In dynamically changing environments, A* path planning enables real-time path replanning while avoiding multiple independently swimming 5 μm spherical Janus micromotors. Finally, the microbot selectively captures multiple cargo particles and autonomously transports and delivers them to a predefined location while simultaneously avoiding dynamic obstacles. These results establish an integrated platform combining programmable trajectory control, autonomous path planning, real-time environmental adaptation, and task execution within a single light-driven Janus microbot system.

papers.title: monoprop: Scaling Pauli and Majorana propagation via Anticommutation Indices
papers.abstract: We introduce monoprop, an open-source, massively parallel operator-propagation framework for fermion and qubit bases. For $N$ qubits or modes, existing codes represent each of the $K$ tracked operator terms (Pauli strings or products of Majorana operators) as a $2N$-bit string, testing each for anticommutation with the gate at $O(KN)$ cost per gate. Here, we introduce the anticommutation index which rapidly looks up the terms anticommuting with a gate. A local gate changes only the terms that touch its sites, and when terms are truncated to act on few sites, only a fraction $\sim1/N$ touch any given qubit or mode, and we use this to prove the time per gate scales as $O(K/N)$. This counterintuitive result tells us that for a fixed number of terms, increasing the number of sites can make things faster. We demonstrate this numerically, and show monoprop scales almost ideally to 8192 cores, tracking $9.5\times10^{10}$ terms. Beyond propagation, we present memory-efficient surrogate graphs, which record one propagation and replay it at new angles, for fast energy re-estimation and parameter gradients, and an efficient method for finding energy-minimising gates and optimal angles for simulating adaptive quantum-chemistry circuits.

papers.title: Equality of the Jellium and the Uniform Electron Gas Energies
papers.abstract: Jellium, a system of electrons in a uniform neutralizing background, and the uniform electron gas (UEG), a system of electrons with constant density and no background, are two standard models of the electron gas. We prove that the ground-state energy per unit volume of Jellium, as defined by Lieb and Narnhofer, coincides with the UEG energy defined by Lewin, Lieb and Seiringer, i.e. \[ e^\hbar_{\rm Jel}(ρ_0)=e^\hbar_{\rm UEG}(ρ_0). \] This equality was previously established in the classical case by Lewin, Lieb and Seiringer and independently by Cotar and Petrache.

papers.title: The Magic Barrier: A Universal Feature of Quantum Thermalization
papers.abstract: We show that the emergence of a ``magic barrier'', characterized by a transient maximum of nonstabilizerness during rapid entanglement growth, is a universal feature of thermalization within quantum ergodic theories, which is intimately connected to random matrix spectral properties. Starting from a pure product state, we analytically determine the time evolution of entanglement entropy, antiflatness, capacity of entanglement, and nonlocal trace distance magic under unitary dynamics generated by random matrix Hamiltonians drawn from all three Gaussian ensembles. We find that the transient maxima of antiflatness, capacity of entanglement, and nonlocal magic occur on the same characteristic timescale as the maximum rate of entanglement growth. These results establish that the magic barrier is a universal feature of RMT thermalization, suggesting universality across quantum chaotic systems. We conclude that quantitative simulations of thermalization in ergodic quantum theories inherently require quantum computation.

papers.title: Standard and Bipolar Rectification in Tilted Periodically-Driven Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: Developing mechanisms to control transport in correlated quantum systems is essential for advancing quantum circuit technologies. In this work, we establish a rectification mechanism for both particle and energy flow in a fermionic system coupled to external baths, in the presence of a tilted potential modulated locally by a time-periodic drive. The drive generates particle and energy currents even in the absence of chemical or thermal bias between the baths. These drive-induced currents are enhanced at resonant frequencies at which avoided crossings occur in the Floquet quasienergy spectrum, reflecting the role of the Floquet states as intermediate channels for transport. Once a bias between the baths is introduced, the drive-induced current contribution can reinforce, compete with, or even cancel the bias-induced contribution. These effects enable rectification in the non-interacting regime, which we quantify via the rectification coefficient $\mathcal{R}$. This coefficient measures the asymmetry between transport up the tilt (forward bias) and down the tilt (reverse bias). In addition to standard rectification, where transport is reduced under reverse bias, we identify a regime of bipolar rectification, in which the current flows only up the tilt regardless of the bias polarity. At the boundary between standard and bipolar regimes, the system achieves perfect rectification, corresponding to complete suppression of the reverse-bias current. In the presence of interactions between particles, the parameter region that supports bipolar rectification is enlarged and $\mathcal{R}$ can be enhanced by many orders of magnitude. Our results establish a rectification mechanism for particle and energy transport that can be experimentally realized in condensed matter and cold atom systems.

papers.title: Platelet-driven contraction enlarges accessible space in layered fibrin networks without uniformly accelerating particle escape
papers.abstract: Platelet traction contracts fibrin networks, yet whether contraction promotes or hinders the escape of suspended particles is unclear. We coupled an overdamped Langevin model of platelet--fibrin mechanics to Brownian transport of finite-size tracers through frozen network states. Nine mechanical replicas were evolved at four filopodial traction baselines (0--8.8\,nN), stacked into 5-$μ$m-thick domains of 50 layers and probed at 0--15\,s with 0.5-$μ$m tracers (29,952 trajectories, 100\,s observation). Benchmarked against experimental clot-contraction kinetics, the simulated contraction is post-lag, within one order of magnitude of experimental rates and corresponds to the onset of the contraction phase. Relative to the matched zero-baseline control, every active-baseline state showed greater projected contraction and a larger tracer-accessible volume ($+9.3\%$ to $+27.6\%$; exact sign test $p=0.0039$ per condition). At 15\,s, mean survival at 100\,s fell from 27.3\% to 14.3\% and the restricted mean exit time from 56.5 to 44.0\,s between the lowest and highest baseline, and all nine replicas shortened residence at 8.8\,nN. At lower baselines, responses differed among replicas, and nearly all retained tracers with a classified start were connected to an exit. Contraction therefore enlarges accessible space without uniformly accelerating escape, separating geometric accommodation from transport kinetics.

papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：血小板牵拉引起的纤维蛋白网络收缩究竟促进还是阻碍悬浮颗粒的逃逸？
证据与比较：九个力学副本、四种丝状伪足牵拉基线（0–8.8 nN）、50层5-μm厚域、0.5-μm示踪颗粒、29,952条轨迹、100 s观测；相对零基线对照，可及体积增加9.3%–27.6%（每条件精确符号检验p=0.0039）；15 s时，最低与最高基线间100 s平均存活率由27.3%降至14.3%，限制平均逃逸时间由56.5 s降至44.0 s。
papers.method_zh: 过阻尼朗之万模型描述血小板–纤维蛋白力学，耦合有限尺寸示踪颗粒在冻结网络态中的布朗输运，并以实验凝块收缩动力学基准校验。

english_guide.finding: Platelet-driven contraction enlarges the tracer-accessible volume but does not uniformly accelerate particle escape, separating geometric accommodation from transport kinetics.
english_guide.question: Does platelet traction-induced fibrin network contraction promote or hinder the escape of suspended particles?
english_guide.evidence: Nine mechanical replicas at four filopodial traction baselines (0–8.8 nN), 50 layers in 5-μm domains, 0.5-μm tracers, 29,952 trajectories, 100 s observation; accessible volume increased by 9.3%–27.6% versus zero-baseline control (exact sign test p=0.0039 per condition); at 15 s, mean survival at 100 s fell from 27.3% to 14.3% and restricted mean exit time from 56.5 to 44.0 s between lowest and highest baseline.
english_guide.method: Overdamped Langevin model of platelet–fibrin mechanics coupled to Brownian transport of finite-size tracers through frozen network states, benchmarked against experimental clot-contraction kinetics.
english_guide.novelty: The authors state that contraction enlarges accessible space without uniformly accelerating escape, separating geometric accommodation from transport kinetics.
english_guide.limitations: Findings rely on simulated frozen network states and specific parameter ranges; the abstract does not specify experimental validation scope, other particle sizes, or network conditions.

papers.novelty_zh: 作者称将几何容纳与输运动力学分离，并表明收缩扩大可及空间却不一致加速逃逸。
papers.limitations_zh: 结论基于模拟冻结网络态与特定参数范围；摘要未说明实验验证范围、其他颗粒尺寸或网络条件。

papers.title: Ergodic topology sampling toward the continuum with Stochastic Normalizing Flows
papers.abstract: In this work we provide numerical evidence that topological freezing in $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ Yang-Mills theory can be mitigated with a flow-based approach, as tested at lattice spacings as fine as 0.03~fm. We do so by analyzing the scaling of the costs of a computational strategy based on the combination of open boundary conditions and Stochastic Normalizing Flows. We show that the integrated autocorrelation time of the squared topological charge and the statistical uncertainty on the topological susceptibility remain under control throughout the explored parameter range with currently available computational resources. This marks an important step toward the use of even more efficient flow-based architectures for ergodic sampling of topology in state-of-the-art lattice gauge theory calculations.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：计算；摘要报告数值证据与成本标度分析；研究对象：SU(3) Yang-Mills 理论格点规范场论中的拓扑采样
papers.abstract_summary_zh: 结合开边界条件与 Stochastic Normalizing Flows 的策略，在格距细至 0.03 fm 时仍能控制拓扑荷平方的自相关时间与拓扑磁化率统计误差。
papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：能否用基于流的采样方法缓解 SU(3) Yang-Mills 理论中的拓扑冻结，并使其成本随格距细化保持可控？
证据与比较：摘要报告在格距细至 0.03 fm 的数值测试中，拓扑荷平方的积分自相关时间与拓扑磁化率的统计不确定度在所探索参数范围内保持受控，并分析了该策略的计算成本标度。
papers.method_zh: 采用开边界条件与 Stochastic Normalizing Flows 相结合的格点计算策略，并分析其成本标度。

english_guide.finding: Numerical evidence is reported that topological freezing in SU(3) Yang-Mills theory can be mitigated with a flow-based approach at lattice spacings as fine as 0.03 fm.
english_guide.question: Can a flow-based strategy combining open boundary conditions and Stochastic Normalizing Flows keep topology sampling costs under control as the lattice spacing is refined?
english_guide.evidence: The integrated autocorrelation time of the squared topological charge and the statistical uncertainty on the topological susceptibility remain under control throughout the explored parameter range with currently available computational resources.
english_guide.method: A computational strategy combining open boundary conditions with Stochastic Normalizing Flows, analyzed through the scaling of its costs.
english_guide.novelty: The authors describe this as an important step toward using even more efficient flow-based architectures for ergodic sampling of topology in state-of-the-art lattice gauge theory calculations.
english_guide.limitations: The abstract does not specify lattice volumes, sample sizes, or error criteria; conclusions are limited to the explored parameter range and currently available computational resources.

papers.limitations_zh: 摘要未明确说明格点体积、统计样本量及误差判据；结论限于所探索参数范围与当前可用计算资源。

papers.title: Surviving readout errors and incomplete postselection in monitored quantum circuits
papers.abstract: We study how readout errors affect dynamics in monitored quantum circuits. Such errors make postselection effectively incomplete, conditioning trajectories on imperfect rather than true records. Focusing on U(1)-symmetric circuits, we find that the charge-sharpening transition survives at a finite error rate, with the sharp phase's vanishing fluctuations replaced by a finite steady-state plateau. The charge fluctuations show a shallow minimum near the ideal transition point as a function of measurement rate, signaling the competition between measurement-induced purification and noise-induced mixing. By decomposing the fluctuations into quantum and classical contributions, we show the minimum marks where incomplete postselection still retains enough trajectory memory to attenuate noise-induced mixing, leaving a detectable signature of the transition even in a noisy setting. Mid-circuit measurements are far harder to mitigate against readout errors than standard end-of-circuit ones, because the errors corrupt the postselection itself; the decomposition therefore offers a minimal mitigation framework and a route to locate the transition directly from experimental data. Our results show that charge sharpening survives readout errors in a quantitative and experimentally accessible way.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：理论/计算；研究监测量子线路中读出误差下的动力学；研究对象：U(1)对称监测量子线路（monitored quantum circuits）
papers.abstract_summary_zh: 在有限读出误差率下电荷锐化转变（charge-sharpening transition）仍然存在，锐相涨落消失被有限稳态平台取代。
papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：读出误差使后选择（postselection）不完整时，监测量子线路中的电荷锐化转变是否存活、如何从涨落中识别。
证据与比较：电荷涨落随测量率在理想转变点附近呈浅极小；将涨落分解为量子和经典贡献，显示极小处不完整后选择仍保留足够轨迹记忆以削弱噪声诱导混合。
papers.method_zh: 针对U(1)对称监测量子线路，将电荷涨落分解为量子与经典贡献，分析测量率依赖及读出误差影响。

english_guide.finding: Charge sharpening survives at finite readout error rate; the sharp phase's vanishing fluctuations become a finite steady-state plateau.
english_guide.question: Does the charge-sharpening transition survive when readout errors make postselection incomplete, and how can it be identified from fluctuations?
english_guide.evidence: Charge fluctuations show a shallow minimum near the ideal transition as a function of measurement rate; decomposing fluctuations into quantum and classical contributions shows the minimum marks where incomplete postselection retains enough trajectory memory to attenuate noise-induced mixing.
english_guide.method: For U(1)-symmetric monitored quantum circuits, charge fluctuations are decomposed into quantum and classical contributions, analyzing measurement-rate dependence and readout-error effects.
english_guide.novelty: The authors state the decomposition offers a minimal mitigation framework and a route to locate the transition directly from experimental data; charge sharpening survives readout errors in a quantitatively and experimentally accessible way.
english_guide.limitations: The abstract does not specify error-model details, numerical parameters, or an upper bound on error rate; the full text was not read, so quantitative claims cannot be verified.

papers.novelty_zh: 作者称分解提供最小缓解框架，并可从实验数据直接定位转变；表明电荷锐化以可实验访问的方式在读出误差下存活。

papers.title: Region bounds, error margins and certified positivity in the numerical conformal bootstrap; Or the first mathematically rigorous bounds on the 3d Ising CFT critical exponents
papers.abstract: Numerical conformal bootstrap bounds are commonly called rigorous, yet as published they are not theorems: they hold at sampled points rather than on regions of parameter space, for truncated rational approximations of the conformal blocks, for a finite list of spins, and up to floating-point rounding. We close all four gaps. We show how to search efficiently for functionals positive on regions, including external-dimension space; how positivity on the large-spin crossing vectors can be imposed as such a region constraint; how new analytic bounds on the conformal-block recursion relations give functionals positive on the true, untruncated crossing vectors; and how to certify the positivity of these functionals in exact arithmetic. The certification rests on Bernstein-basis positivity certificates in up to three variables, exact arithmetic in $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt2)$, a compactified treatment of the infinite spin tail, and an explicit bound on the difference between the true blocks and their truncations, so that infinitely many positivity conditions reduce to finitely many machine-checked sign conditions. As a flagship application we certify an exclusion region in the $(Δ_σ,Δ_ε)$ plane: for $Δ_σ\in[0.505,0.5405]$ all of $Δ_ε\in(1/2,3]$ is excluded except a small rectangle containing the 3d Ising island, giving rigorous two-sided bounds on the critical exponents $η$ and $ν$ under explicitly stated spectrum assumptions. The analytic inputs for the mixed $σ$-$ε$ system, which would remove the spin-2 gap assumption, are also proved. The same methods prevent common practical failure modes and can make bootstrap searches faster: region bounds turn the mapping of an island into a handful of one-dimensional bisections. The essential code to reproduce the search and the certification, and all machine-checkable certificates, are released.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：理论/计算；基于数值共形自举的严格数学证明；研究对象：三维 Ising 共形场论（3d Ising CFT）的临界指数与自举排除区域
papers.abstract_summary_zh: 在明确谱假设下，对三维 Ising CFT 的临界指数 η 和 ν 给出数学严格的双侧界，并认证 (Δ_σ,Δ_ε) 平面中的排除区域。
papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：如何把数值共形自举中通常被称为严格、但实际只在采样点、截断共形块、有限自旋表和浮点舍入下成立的界，提升为真正的定理。
证据与比较：认证 Δ_σ∈[0.505,0.5405] 时，除含 3d Ising island 的小矩形外，Δ_ε∈(1/2,3] 全部被排除；据此在明确谱假设下得到 η、ν 的严格双侧界，并给出机器可检验的正性证书。
papers.method_zh: 区域正性泛函搜索、大自旋交叉向量区域约束、共形块递推关系解析界、Bernstein 基正性证书、Q(√2) 精确算术、无穷自旋尾紧化及截断误差显式界。

english_guide.finding: Under explicitly stated spectrum assumptions, rigorous two-sided bounds on the 3d Ising CFT critical exponents η and ν are certified, with an exclusion region in the (Δ_σ,Δ_ε) plane.
english_guide.question: How to turn numerical conformal bootstrap bounds, commonly called rigorous but holding only at sampled points, for truncated conformal blocks, finite spin lists and floating-point rounding, into actual theorems.
english_guide.evidence: For Δ_σ∈[0.505,0.5405], all Δ_ε∈(1/2,3] is excluded except a small rectangle containing the 3d Ising island; machine-checkable positivity certificates are provided.
english_guide.method: Region-positivity functional search, large-spin crossing vector region constraints, analytic bounds on conformal-block recursion, Bernstein-basis positivity certificates, exact arithmetic in Q(√2), compactified infinite spin tail, explicit truncation error bounds.
english_guide.novelty: Authors claim to close four rigor gaps: regions rather than sampled points, true rather than truncated blocks, infinite spin tail, and exact-arithmetic certification; analytic inputs for the mixed σ-ε system removing the spin-2 gap assumption are also proved.
english_guide.limitations: Results rely on spectrum assumptions explicitly stated in the abstract; specific numerical intervals for η and ν are not given; other physical approximations beyond finite spin truncation are not addressed.

papers.novelty_zh: 作者声称补上四个严格性缺口：区域而非采样点、真共形块而非截断、无穷自旋尾、精确算术认证；并证明可去除 spin-2 gap 假设的混合 σ-ε 解析输入。

papers.title: Crystallization of the undertile
papers.abstract: We classify all periodic tilings with a monotile known as $\mathbf{R1}$ and called here the undertile, which underlies several aperiodic monotiles such as the Taylor-Socolar one. The classification is done using deflation, through a study of fracture lines between zones where deflation can be performed. A full classification of fracture patterns is given, that also applies to non-periodic tilings with the undertile. This can be used to reprove non-periodicity of some existing monotiles based on the undertile.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：理论/数学分类研究；依据摘要中的分类与deflation分析；研究对象：undertile（R1）单块铺砌及其周期与非周期铺砌
papers.abstract_summary_zh: 借助deflation与fracture line分析，完整分类了undertile R1的所有周期铺砌，并给出适用于非周期铺砌的fracture pattern完整分类。
papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：如何对以R1 undertile构成的全部周期铺砌进行分类，并刻画deflation区域间fracture line结构？
证据与比较：摘要称给出全部周期铺砌的分类，并给出fracture pattern的完整分类；该分类也适用于非周期铺砌，可用于重新证明若干基于undertile的monotile的非周期性。摘要未提供具体铺砌数量或定量比较。
papers.method_zh: 使用deflation方法，研究可执行deflation的区域之间的fracture line，并分类fracture pattern。

english_guide.question: How can all periodic tilings with the R1 undertile be classified via deflation and fracture lines?
english_guide.evidence: The abstract states a full classification of periodic tilings and of fracture patterns, applicable also to non-periodic tilings; no counts or quantitative comparisons are provided.
english_guide.method: Deflation, studying fracture lines between zones where deflation can be performed, and classifying fracture patterns.
english_guide.novelty: The authors claim a full classification of periodic tilings with the undertile and of fracture patterns applicable to non-periodic tilings.
english_guide.limitations: The abstract does not specify applicability boundaries or proof details; the RSS snippet may be truncated, and no quantitative data are given.
